items.title: Grünkohl Quiche
items.prompt: Close-up of a whole 28 cm kale quiche for ten servings, removed from its tin and cut into ten wedges on a large white serving platter, one wedge slightly separated to reveal the cut face. A crisp, golden-brown spelt shortcrust base and 3 cm-high rim have a light wholemeal speckle. The generous filling is predominantly curly kale, using 450 g raw leaves that collapse during covered braising: soft, deep olive-green torn leaves with small translucent onion and garlic pieces, bound in firm, moist, pale creamy-yellow custard from three eggs, 200 g sour cream, 150 ml cream and mustard. Of 150 g grated cheese, two-thirds melts through the custard and the rest forms a slightly uneven golden-brown, lightly crisp top. Fifty grams of irregular tan walnut kernels are scattered across the filling, lightly pressed in and roasted by baking, some visible beneath the cheese. The exposed cut side shows compact dark-green kale and set custard above the pastry base. Bright soft natural daylight, crisp detail and true colours; camera at about 65 degrees, food filling the square frame with platter edges cropped. Calm warm-light wood background with only a small natural linen napkin edge and clean unmarked surfaces.

items.title: Grünkohlpfanne
items.prompt: Close-up of a generous family-style kale, potato and lean bacon pan for four in its large frying pan, with chilled garlic-feta yogurt alongside. Curly kale leaves stripped from thick ribs form an abundant, juicy tangle of rich dark green with olive tones, fully collapsed, tender and glossy from covered simmering, with soft curled surfaces. Finely chopped pale-green ribs and tiny soft garlic pieces sit within the leaves. Halved small boiled potatoes are folded throughout and clearly visible across the surface, showing moist yellow flesh, thin pale-tan skin on curved edges, and golden to deep-brown seared patches. Small lean bacon dice are rosy and glossy with lightly browned edges. Light cooking juices moisten the base. Beside the pan, a plain white bowl holds the substantial chilled accompaniment: thick, spoonable off-white yogurt flecked with small soft feta curds, finely chopped raw garlic and black pepper. The potatoes remain mixed through the greens, and the sauce stays alongside. A serving spoon rests in the pan. At a 65-degree angle, the food fills most of the square frame; pan edges are cropped and part of the sauce bowl is visible. Bright soft natural daylight, crisp detail, true rich greens and golden browns, gentle steam, a clean unmarked pale warm-wood surface.

items.title: Winter-Minestrone mit Grünkohl
items.prompt: Close-up of one deep white bowl of hot, brothy vegetable, white-bean, smoked-sausage and kale soup, showing one generous individual serving. Ample clear to lightly cloudy golden broth surrounds many plump, smooth-skinned ivory beans, softened small orange carrot dice, pale celery-green dice and translucent onion pieces. Round sausage coins have dark reddish-brown casings, deep rose-red interiors and tiny pale fat flecks; they look moist and tender from simmering, their sliced shape intact. A substantial yet reduced tangle of dark forest-green to olive kale, torn into small uneven pieces, is fully wilted, silky and crinkled after blanching and simmering. A few softened pale garlic fragments and the seasonings recede into the broth. Following the recipe, everything is ladled together into the bowl, beans and sausage visible throughout and greens woven between them. A small amount of finely grated pale-ivory Parmesan is lightly scattered over the surface, just beginning to soften. Faint steam and isolated golden oil glints show that it is freshly served. Photographed from a 70-degree angle, the bowl fills most of a square frame against a plain pale warm-wood table, with the rim partly cropped. Bright soft natural daylight, crisp detail and true colours show the brothy consistency and every component clearly.

items.title: Szegediner Gulasch
items.prompt: Close-up of one generous individual serving of finished Szegediner goulash in a wide off-white deep bowl: bite-sized pork braised with abundant sauerkraut in creamy paprika-tomato sauce, finished with sour cream and parsley. Irregular pork shoulder pieces retain golden-to-deep-brown seared patches and look moist and tender after the covered simmer, softly coated rather than crisp. Nearly as much softened sauerkraut appears as supple, tangled pale-straw ribbons stained peach and brick red. The generous glossy terracotta-orange to brick-red sauce is lightly reduced and spoon-coating yet pools loosely around the solids; finely diced onion and garlic have mostly melted into it, with sparse dark caraway seeds. A small thick white dollop of reserved sour cream and a restrained fresh parsley garnish sit on top. The stew is casually ladled and generously fills the bowl, with a modest clean rim and faint natural steam. A 65-degree camera angle, bright soft natural daylight, crisp detail and true colours show every component clearly. The bowl dominates the square frame against calm pale warm wood, its outer edges slightly cropped; the setting is clean and unmarked, with no extra food, text, logos, hands or people.

items.title: Schweine-Rahm-Gulasch
items.prompt: Close-up of a generous family-style serving for four: tender braised pork in creamy paprika sauce with a large batch of boiled flour dumplings. Abundant pork shoulder pieces, cut as 2.5 cm cubes and now slightly irregular, are opaque and tender, with tan-brown seared patches showing through the glossy sauce. A large quantity of collapsed pale-golden onion wedges and strands is partly melted into it, while a smaller quantity of skin-on diamond-cut red peppers remains soft but recognisable and vividly red. Tomato paste, hot paprika and sour cream give the lightly starch-thickened sauce a velvety orange-red colour and creamy highlights; it coats the meat and pools beneath it rather than becoming broth. Beside and partly nestled into the goulash sits a substantial heap of irregular spoon-cut dumplings from the egg-milk-flour dough, plump and cooked through, ivory-cream with moist, softly rough boiled surfaces. Everything is arranged together in one wide, shallow white serving bowl, with pork, peppers and dumplings clearly visible and a large serving spoon resting in the saucy side. Bright soft natural daylight, a 65-degree camera angle, crisp detail and true colours; abundant food fills nearly all the square frame, with the bowl edges slightly cropped. Subtle steam, a calm pale warm-wood background and a small natural linen edge complete the clean, unmarked, ungarnished setting.

items.title: Spekulatius-Apfel-Tiramisu
items.prompt: Close-up of a whole, uncut chilled four-serving layered apple dessert in its small 15 x 20 cm clear glass baking dish. A thin base of rectangular spice biscuits is darkened and softened by espresso, topped with a generous layer of fully cooled apple compote: peeled, irregularly diced apples simmered until tender but still recognisable, pale honey-gold with lightly syrupy juices and fine cinnamon specks. Above this sits a thick, smooth pale-ivory mascarpone and whipped-cream layer flecked with tiny vanilla seeds. The level top has a light dusting of cocoa and four dry, crisp, embossed brown biscuits resting flat on it. Through the near glass side, the moist biscuit base, fruit layer and cream remain distinct in their original order. The dessert fills most of the square frame, with the dish edges partly cropped. A 65-degree camera angle shows both the cocoa-dusted surface and the side layers. Bright soft natural daylight gives crisp detail and true-to-life colours, against a calm pale warm-wood surface with clean, unmarked surroundings.

items.title: Spekulatius-Tiramisu
items.prompt: Close-up of the whole chilled Spekulatius-Tiramisu for four, uncut in its small transparent rectangular 20 × 15 cm glass dish. Two thick layers of smooth, softly set ivory quark–mascarpone cream dominate, with faint cinnamon warmth and tiny orange-zest flecks. Between them sits a thinner, juicy layer of thawed deep-ruby raspberries, their soft whole and slightly collapsed shapes held in a little red syrup that lightly stains the adjoining cream. Thin rectangular spice-brown biscuits form the bottom and middle layers, now tender and cake-like from chilling, visible through the glass rather than crisp. The upper cream is smoothly spread with subtle spatula marks and a fine matte cocoa–cinnamon dusting surrounding a sharply defined, undusted pale star left by the lifted stencil. A restrained optional garnish of red raspberries and small fresh mint leaves rests at one corner without obscuring the pattern. The generously filled dish nearly reaches the edges of the square frame. Photographed at about 65 degrees so both the patterned top and distinct side layers are clear, in bright soft natural daylight with crisp detail and true-to-life colours. Pale warm wood and a narrow edge of natural linen create a calm, clean, unmarked background.

items.title: Lebkuchen Tiramisu
items.prompt: Close-up of a whole chilled, family-style layered dessert for eight in a high-rimmed rectangular 15 x 25 cm baking dish, with one cut portion raised on a dessert server to reveal the layers. A generous amount of thick, smoothly whipped ivory mascarpone-quark cream, delicately freckled with cinnamon and fine orange zest, dominates two thinner layers of soft medium-brown gingerbread. The gingerbread hearts, pretzels and stars were split horizontally; their porous cut faces are patchily darkened and moistened by the sweetened coffee-amaretto drizzle while staying coherent. Between them sits a glossy, deep ruby-burgundy cherry compote; plump, softened dark-red cherries remain recognisable in lightly thickened juice. Inside the dish, the order is moist gingerbread, cream, cherry compote, cream, a second moist gingerbread layer, then the remaining cream spread flat. A fine, even dry dusting of cocoa covers the top in a matte cocoa-brown veil; the lifted piece shows all layers neatly set after chilling. The cocoa-covered dessert nearly fills the square frame, with the white ceramic dish edges cropped and a plain silver server as the only utensil. Photograph at a 65-degree angle in bright, soft natural daylight with crisp detail and true colours. A calm pale warm-wood table and a small edge of natural linen form a clean, unmarked background; the dessert looks cool, generously portioned and homemade.

items.title: Pichelsteiner Eintopf mit Steakwürfeln
items.prompt: Close-up of a whole family-style batch of hearty German mixed-meat and vegetable stew for four, still in its large cooking pot, with abundant broth and clearly visible solids. The largest solid share is mixed soup vegetables: orange carrot rounds and chunks, pale ivory celery pieces and tender white-and-pale-green leek rings, all intact after brief cooking. Equal modest amounts of dark-brown beef and opaque grey-beige pork cubes, plus a smaller share of pale-tan veal, sit among a modest amount of cream-yellow, just-tender peeled potato cubes and collapsed pale-gold onion strips. Beef shows soft seared patches from brief browning; all meats look fully cooked, moist and tender. Everything is surrounded and lightly coated by generous, thin amber-brown meat broth, with a delicate melted-fat sheen and tiny marjoram and black-pepper flecks. Finely chopped fresh parsley is lightly scattered over the surface. Served family-style in a pale cream enamel pot, with a plain metal ladle resting at one side and the solids naturally mixed throughout. The pot fills nearly the entire square frame, its rim cropped, on a clean unmarked warm light-wood surface. A camera angle of about 65 degrees, bright soft natural daylight, crisp moist detail, true vegetable colours and a wisp of steam complete the calm, appetising scene.
